notes: A is the arguments of the example call `import numpy as np ; rs = np.random.RandomState(50) ; x = rs.uniform(-1., 1., (5, 5)) ; x += np.diag(np.abs(x).sum(axis=1) + 1.) ; factorMatrix0(x)`. Changed for Q32: A and B are seeded strictly diagonally dominant 5x5 matrices (each diagonal entry exceeds the rest of its row by at least 1, so every pivot stays away from 0) instead of upstream's np.arange(1., 26.).reshape(5, 5), which is singular (rank 2) and gives an exact zero pivot in Q32. B is the arguments of `import numpy as np ; rs = np.random.RandomState(51) ; x = rs.uniform(-1., 1., (5, 5)) ; x += np.diag(np.abs(x).sum(axis=1) + 1.) ; factorMatrix0(x)`.
